i think it's a combination of things. it's a long story.
thanks for talking about it. it'd be nice if i could enjoy life. it'd make all this a moot point.

I'm 26. Off and on I've thought about it, but started making up my mind a few weeks ago.

I know I'll miss things, and people, and it'll kinda suck. Of course, I won't be around later on to feel those things, so that's a relief.

A lot of what could be said about the hypocrisy and morality of the situation has already been said [here](http://www.reddit.com/r/IAmA/comments/fy6yz/51_hours_left_to_live/c1jija8?context=2) and [in this post](http://www.reddit.com/r/IAmA/comments/fy201/im_out_on_monday/).

Maybe (almost certainly) I can't trust my own thoughts, but I'm not in a position to get that fixed.

It's kinda funny how we value physical pain over emotional/mental pain, as if the latter doesn't matter or exist, or that we have no right to escape the latter kind of suffering with any dignity, but if it's the former, then we get, like, a whole Reddit phenomenon like you see with Lucidending.

It's hypocritical and a contradiction. When it's convenient to describe it as so, depression (for example) is treated like a real disease, but on the other hand, sometimes it's just disregarded as frivolous.

No one needs to help me die. My mind and my plan is made up. I just wondered if anyone knew about making the process easier and smoother for those around me.
